messages:
Anika (support): Hey team — customer reporting structured JSON mode over streaming gets truncated ~70% of the time. They see a partial object like '{\"id\":123,\"items\":[{...},' and then connection closes.
customer-acct-ops: repro steps: we hit /v1/generate with 'Accept: text/event-stream' and stream:true. Happens on our prod behind ALB + nginx sidecar. No consistent sequence length.
customer-acct-ops: sample last chunk from client TCP dump (base64): '...7b226964223a3132332c226974656d73223a5b7b2274' which decodes to partial JSON and then TCP FIN.
Anika (support): Thanks — can you paste the exact curl/node repro you used? Also whether you use gzip/transfer-encoding?
customer-acct-ops: curl we used:
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-xyz","stream":true,"prompt":"..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
We also have node fetch using AbortController where we stream body.getReader().read().
Felix (eng): Does the truncated output always end mid-token/byte or sometimes right after a complete JSON value? If mid-byte it's likely connection close/partial chunk.
customer-acct-ops: always mid-JSON, sometimes ends in the middle of a UTF-8 multi-byte sequence (we see replacement chars when tried to parse). Not reproducible locally - only seen through customer's infra stack.
Raj (sre): Common culprits: ALB idle timeout, nginx buffering or gzip spraying, or the sidecar killing idle streams. ALB default idle is 60s. If the model stalls (no tokens) ALB may close and client sees EOF mid-JSON.
Anika (support): Can you attach nginx logs and ALB access logs for one failed request? Also indicate whether you use HTTP keepalive between sidecar and API.
customer-acct-ops: attached small snippet of ALB log in thread (omitted here), shows target: 200 and received_bytes < sent_bytes and 'timed out' weirdness. nginx conf: proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 60s; gzip on; proxy_set_header Connection "";
Felix (eng): Gzip with chunked streams can cause proxies to buffer until gzip block finishes; if proxy buffers and then is killed, you get truncated chunks. Suggest turning off gzip for SSE endpoints. Also ensure proxy_read_timeout > expected stall.
Raj (sre): Quick repro we ran: run a local python server that streams JSON objects slowly, put nginx as reverse proxy with gzip on and proxy_read_timeout 10s, client gets truncated JSON when idle > 10s. We can share diff.
deploy-bot: deploy finished: disable-gzip-sse -> staging (ok).
Anika (support): Customer, can you try temporarily disabling gzip in your sidecar and increasing proxy_read_timeout to 120s to see if failures stop?
customer-acct-ops: Trying now, will report in 30m.
customer-acct-ops: Quick update — after disabling gzip the truncation rate dropped dramatically in a 1h smoke. Still saw 1 failure where ALB closed idle connection at 60s.
Felix (eng): Two mitigation options for streaming structured JSON: 1) add an end sentinel in the stream (e.g. an explicit final SSE event with 'event: end' and the full JSON assembled on client side), or 2) send smaller JSON frames that are self-contained (JSON Lines) so partial frames never produce invalid JSON. Both require client changes.
Anika (support): Also documented workaround: use non-streaming responses when you need guaranteed parseable JSON, or implement client-side buffering until EOF and robust UTF-8 handling. We'll add guidance to docs.
Raj (sre): Product note for eng: consider offering a small header (e.g. X-Stream-Heartbeat: 15s) where server emits keepalive SSE comment lines ':\n' to prevent idle timeouts across proxies. This helped with ALB.
Felix (eng): Filed a short RFC: #4621 stream-heartbeat + guidance on gzip/streaming.
customer-acct-ops: Thanks all — disabling gzip + bumping timeouts + adding client buffer removed the failures for us. We'll re-open if we see more. :thumbsup:
Anika (support): Closing ticket tentatively. If you want, we can assist in adding sentinel wrapper or switch to JSONL on your client.
customer-acct-ops: Appreciate it, will take you up on help for JSONL migration next week.
